tasks.title: [r2-retry-status] isRetryableR2Status: which R2 reply statuses are worth retrying
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/r2-retry-status.ts` exporting `isRetryableR2Status(status: number): boolean`.

Behavior: given the HTTP status code of a reply from R2, answer true when the request is worth retrying and false when it is not. Worth retrying: 429 (too many requests) and every server error status from 500 through 599. Not worth retrying: everything else, including success, redirect and other client error statuses, and anything above 599.

tasks.title: [r2-retry-delay] r2RetryDelayMs: bounded backoff for an R2 retry attempt
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/r2-retry-delay.ts` exporting `r2RetryDelayMs(attempt: number, baseMs: number): number`.

Behavior: how many milliseconds to wait before retry number `attempt` (counting from 0), given a base wait of `baseMs`. Attempt 0 waits exactly the base. Each later attempt waits longer than the one before, following the pattern in the examples. The wait is never more than 30000 ms, whatever the attempt or base. A base of 0 always gives 0.

Examples (attempt, baseMs gives wait):
- 0, 1000 gives 1000
- 1, 1000 gives 4000
- 2, 1000 gives 9000
- 3, 1000 gives 16000
- 4, 1000 gives 25000
- 5, 1000 gives 30000
- 10, 1000 gives 30000
- 100, 1000 gives 30000
- 0, 500 gives 500
- 1, 500 gives 2000
- 2, 250 gives 2250
- 0, 0 gives 0
- 7, 0 gives 0
- 0, 40000 gives 30000

Context (Builder pre-file, refile of #487, behavior only): Peace's task (source: peace). The future R2 retry needs a wait that grows per attempt and never exceeds 30 seconds, so one retry cannot stall a scan. This issue states only the wanted behavior and example cases; PeaceAI has to work out the implementation itself. tasks.title: [health-checkin-line] checkinLine: the plain-text health check-in line a scanner part writes
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/health-checkin-line.ts` exporting `checkinLine(part: string, status: string, note: string): string`.

Behavior: the one plain-text health check-in line a scanner part writes for the health module. The line is the word CHECKIN, then the part name, then the status word, then the note with the key facts or the error, each separated from the one before by a single vertical bar, in that order. The pieces are copied exactly as given, with nothing trimmed or changed, so an empty piece still keeps its bar.

Examples (part, status, note gives line):
- "scan", "OK", "rows 812" gives "CHECKIN|scan|OK|rows 812"
- "tenmin", "ERROR", "R2_GET_500" gives "CHECKIN|tenmin|ERROR|R2_GET_500"
- "gap-refill", "OK", "" gives "CHECKIN|gap-refill|OK|"
- "Daily Bars", "WARN", "late 3m" gives "CHECKIN|Daily Bars|WARN|late 3m"
- "r2", "ERROR", " timeout " gives "CHECKIN|r2|ERROR| timeout "
- "", "OK", "no part" gives "CHECKIN||OK|no part"
- "intraday2", "", "missing status" gives "CHECKIN|intraday2||missing status"
- " backfill", "Ok", "done: 4/4" gives "CHECKIN| backfill|Ok|done: 4/4"
- "read-api ", "SILENT", "last 2026-10-24" gives "CHECKIN|read-api |SILENT|last 2026-10-24"
- "Sidecar9", " OK", "count=12, ok" gives "CHECKIN|Sidecar9| OK|count=12, ok"
- "host", "error 2", "fetch failed" gives "CHECKIN|host|error 2|fetch failed"
- "parser", "Bad, 3 ", "x" gives "CHECKIN|parser|Bad, 3 |x"

Context (Builder pre-file, behavior only): Peace's task (source: peace). Slice 1 of Peace's scanner self-health-check system. Peace's spec (2026-10-22): each scanner part writes a small plain-text check-in (status, error, key facts) to one health module; the module flags parts that go silent, error, or report wrong facts, so anyone can see at a glance what is wrong; check-ins are kept for one month and a weekly check reviews that history; Dust is not used for the check-ins. On 2026-10-25 Peace asked the team to pick a real task itself ("I don't can't you guys think of one?"), and this is the one picked. This issue states only the wanted behavior and example cases; PeaceAI has to work out the implementation itself. Production safety: one new function in a new module plus one new test file under src/ only. Nothing imports it yet, so the running scanner, the scan and the ten-minute chain are unchanged. Wiring it into the scanner parts is a separate task.

tasks.title: [health-error-count] countErrorParts: how many scanner parts reported an error
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/health-error-count.ts` exporting `countErrorParts(states: string[]): number`.

Behavior: the at-a-glance count of scanner parts whose last check-in reported an error. Given the state word of every part, answer how many of the words are exactly ERROR, in capitals. A part that has gone silent, shown as SILENT, is not an error: it is counted on its own, as a missing check-in, by a separate task. A state word the health module does not recognize, anything other than OK, SILENT or ERROR, such as WARN or a lower-case error, is never counted as an error either. An empty list gives 0.

Examples (states gives count):
- [] gives 0
- ["OK"] gives 0
- ["ERROR"] gives 1
- ["SILENT"] gives 0
- ["WARN", "error"] gives 0
- ["ERROR", "ERROR", "SILENT", "SILENT"] gives 2
- ["OK", "WARN", "ERROR", "SILENT", "ERROR", "ERROR"] gives 3

Peace's answer to "Should a part that's gone silent count the same as one with an error, or be counted separately?" (Peace, Grok Bot chat with Builder, Oct 26 2026 1:30 PM MT): "it shouldn’t be counted as an error because it something my be wrong with just the health check part but the actual part might still be working but it still should be something that the health check knows it’s missing when it doesn’t get reported so that we can check what is actually going wrong"

Peace's answer to "If a part reports a state word the health module doesn't recognize, how should that be treated?" (Peace, Grok Bot chat with Builder, Oct 26 2026 1:30 PM MT): "it shouldn’t be anything negative the health module should take note of it and we can teach it what it means or if it’s not something we want we can make sure that report can’t happen again and have it report a better word for what’s wrong"

tasks.title: [health-no-response-line] noResponseLine: the message for a scanner part that has not answered the health check
tasks.body:
Target: PeaceG03/PeaceSTOCKS

Add a new module `src/health-no-response-line.ts` exporting `noResponseLine(part: string, requests: number): string`.

Behavior: the message the health module shows for a scanner part it has heard nothing from. Given the part's name and how many times the health check has asked it for a check-in, the message is the words no response from, a space, the part name exactly as given, then a comma, a space, the words requested health check, a space, the number of requests, a space and then the fixed word time followed by a slash and the letter s, the same for every count. The part name is copied exactly as given, with nothing trimmed or changed, and the number is written exactly as given in plain digits, so only the number changes from one message to the next, and a number below zero, which should never happen, keeps its minus sign.

Examples (part, requests gives message):
- "Daily Bars", 45 gives "no response from Daily Bars, requested health check 45 time/s"
- "gap-refill", 1 gives "no response from gap-refill, requested health check 1 time/s"
- "r2", 0 gives "no response from r2, requested health check 0 time/s"
- "read-api ", 7 gives "no response from read-api , requested health check 7 time/s"
- "", 5 gives "no response from , requested health check 5 time/s"
- "intraday2", 1440 gives "no response from intraday2, requested health check 1440 time/s"
- "tenmin", -1 gives "no response from tenmin, requested health check -1 time/s"

Peace's answer to "If no parts have reported at all, what should the health check say?" (Peace, Grok Bot chat with Builder, Oct 26 2026 1:30 PM MT): "something like - “no response from (what part), requested health check X times"

Peace's answer to the follow-up on whether a single request should read 1 times or 1 time (Peace, Grok Bot chat with Builder, Oct 26 2026 2:29 PM MT): "have it with “time/s” just so it doesn’t have to change at all it can be a static word only the number before changes"

Context (Builder pre-file, ADD_FUNCTION, public-derive-from-behavior-v1 template join, behavior only): Team-picked task (Builder-drafted; not credited as source: peace unless Peace says so in his own words); the behavior follows Peace's own answers quoted above. Builder's choices, not Peace's: four parts of this behavior were decided by Builder and are not in Peace's words. First, Peace answered what the health check should say if no parts have reported at all; applying that answer as one message per silent part, built from that one part's name and its own request count, is Builder's reading of his answer. Second, an empty part name is copied as given, so the message reads no response from followed directly by the comma; Peace was not asked about an empty name. Third, a request count below zero keeps its minus sign instead of being refused or changed; Peace was not asked about a negative count. Also, a part name is never trimmed, so 'read-api ' keeps its trailing space in the message; Peace was not asked about this. Any of these can change if Peace says otherwise. Peace's spec (2026-10-22): each scanner part writes a small plain-text check-in (status, error, key facts) to one health module; the module flags parts that go silent, error, or report wrong facts, so anyone can see at a glance what is wrong; check-ins are kept for one month and a weekly check reviews that history; Dust is not used for the check-ins.
